author: Fortenbaugh, W. W.
title: Aristotle on Emotion: A Contribution to Philosophical Psychology, Rhetoric, Poetics, Politics and Ethics
venue: London: Gerald Duckworth & Co. (monograph, ~92 pp. of text)
pole: judgmental (doxastic) — the cognitivist locus classicus and chronological origin of the cluster
ocr_confidence: high (clean-copy text PDF; archive.org scan with light OCR noise in footnotes and Bekker numerals, e.g. 'i378a3o' for 1378a30; running text and printed pagination fully legible; Greek transliterated throughout, no polytonic)
abstract_paraphrase: Fortenbaugh argues that Aristotle, resolving an Academic debate Plato had left open in the Philebus, gave the first genuinely COGNITIVE account of emotion: an emotion essentially INVOLVES A THOUGHT/BELIEF/JUDGMENT, built into its essential definition as the EFFICIENT CAUSE (anger = pain on account of an apparent unjust slight; fear = the appearance of impending evil). Because the cognition is constitutive, emotions are (a) explicable by demonstrative science (cognition as syllogistic middle term), (b) open to reason and rhetorical persuasion (the basis of the Rhetoric's emotional appeal), (c) the matter of intelligent poetic responses (pity/fear/laughter; the rehabilitation of drama vs. Republic X; katharsis), and (d) the foundation of a BIPARTITE political-ethical psychology (alogical/emotional half obedient to the logical/calculative half) that replaces Platonic tripartition and underwrites the moral-virtue / practical-wisdom distinction. Emotions are thereby sharply distinguished from non-rational bodily drives (hunger, thirst, sex), whose efficient cause is physiological. CRITICAL FOR THE CLUSTER AXIS: Fortenbaugh's constitutive cognition is DOXA / KRISIS (belief, judgment, opinion, 'propositional judgment open to reasoned logos'), NOT phantasia; phantasia and 'imagination' appear nowhere in his apparatus or subject index.

outline.summary: Emotion and cognition. The Academic problem (Philebus 47e; opinion 'intimately connected' but the connection unexplained). Aristotle's solution: the thought is the EFFICIENT CAUSE in the essential definition. Topics already prefers a causal definition (anger = pain DIA the thought of outrage, not 'with'/'made of'). Rhetoric fixes anger (1378a30-32) and fear (1382a21-22). Anticipates modern debate (Bedford vs. Pitcher vs. James).

Emotion under demonstrative science (Posterior Analytics): essence = cause; emotion explained syllogistically with cognition as middle term. Corollaries: anger necessarily at a particular individual (belief has an object); emotions logically distinguished by which thought is built in (anger/hate/fear/shame). Inclusive analysis: efficient + material (boiling blood) + final (revenge) cause (De An. 403a25-b2).

Contribution to rhetoric. Deductive ('esto'/let-it-be) method meets Plato's Phaedrus demand. Substantively: belief-as-efficient-cause makes emotion 'intelligent behaviour open to reasoned persuasion'; emotional appeal ceases to be Gorgianic charm/enchantment/drug and becomes coordinate with demonstration; appeals freed from prooemium/epilogue.

Contribution to poetics. Tragedy tied to cognitive fear+pity, comedy to the laughable; Republic X charge dissolved; tragic emotions as plot-controls (1452b34-1453a1); comedy pruned of envy toward Hobbesian superiority/'educated insolence'. Inclusive (cognitive+bodily) analysis grounds homoeopathic katharsis (Poet. 1449b27-28; Pol. 1341b32-1342a15).

A New Political-Ethical Psychology. Laws' latent bipartition (puppet-image golden vs. iron cords; fear/confidence as DOXAI, elpis = opinions about the future, 644c9-d1) read as TWO KINDS OF COGNITION (emotion vs. reflection), not thought-vs-thrust (contra Gorgemanns). Aristotle formalizes alogical/logical halves (EN 1102b13-1103a3); an ADVANCE over tripartition; must NOT be conflated with De Anima's biological sensation/intellect psychology. Emotion has no single biological locus (fear = nous+aisthesis+orexis), which is why De Anima 'ignores' emotion.

Consequences for Political Theory: moral education (paideia trains alogical 'loves and hates' before logos matures, after Laws 653b); imperfection of the young (action-guiding opinions sans phronesis); natural slaves; women. Animal/human boundary policed by the doxa-requirement: animal discrimination is aisthesis+krisis but only 'quasi-affirmation/denial' (De An. 431a9-10), never doxa open to persuasive logos.

A new conception of human virtue: moral virtue = a hexis perfecting man's alogical-but-COGNITIVE half; a peculiarly human virtue (EN 1102a14-16). Even courage is a cognitive disposition (learning to despise/kataphronein danger and to SEE endurance as noble). Animals temperate/courageous only metaphorically (1149b31-32; 1145a25-27).

Virtuous action WITHOUT calculation. The 'more courageous man' (EN 1117a18-22): in sudden alarms no time to deliberate, so response issues from the well-trained alogical half alone; hitting the mean is a quick, logos-less critical act (eustochia, 1142a2-3). The 'right reason' formula commits Aristotle only to reason's AUTHORITY in justification, not its presence in every virtuous act. [Seat of an unreflective-but-cognitive value-assessment.]

Moral virtue and the goal of action: moral virtue makes the END correct, phronesis the MEANS (EN 1144a7-9; 1145a4-6). Habituated opinions set the noble goal; cleverness selects means. Against Allan: moral virtue CAN furnish a true judgment of the end, because the alogical half is itself cognitive (the anti-Humean core).

Practical vs. non-practical emotions. PRACTICAL (fear->safety; anger->revenge, absent when revenge appears impossible, Rhet. 1370b13, 1378b1-4) build a goal into their essence and support action-involving virtues (courage, good temper). NON-PRACTICAL (shame, indignation, pity) carry no essential goal and support NO virtue — hence no 'righteous indignation' virtue and no analogue to Christian mercy.

Temperance and human appetites. Sharpest emotion-vs-DRIVE statement: emotions have a cognitive efficient cause, bodily drives a physiological one. Temperance saved as a virtue via NON-RATIONAL appetite (through the body, not from judgment) vs. RATIONAL appetite (attributed to persuasion) (Rhet. 1370a18-25). Temperate 'loves and hates' are acquired judgment-caused rational appetites obedient to argument; even sexual desire 'often caused by thoughts and beliefs' — 'judgment arouses the body, not vice versa'. Bare hunger is persuasion-proof (1113b26-30).

Non-emotional modes of social interaction: friendliness, wittiness, truthfulness are moral virtues DISSOCIATED from both emotions and appetites — perfections of the alogical half exhibited 'in speech and action'. Shows the alogical half is broader than the emotions; not every hexis of it is emotion-grounded.

concepts.label: emotion essentially involves a thought/belief (the cognitivist thesis)
concepts.gloss: Fortenbaugh's central claim: a pathos has cognition built into its essence; cognition is necessary, not merely characteristic (contra Pitcher/James, with Bedford).

concepts.label: the cognition is the EFFICIENT CAUSE in the essential definition
concepts.gloss: The thought is named in the definition as the cause: anger = pain DIA the thought of an apparent unjust slight (Rhet. 1378a30-32). Not 'with' (meta) but 'on account of' (dia) — settled in Top. 150b27-151a19.

concepts.label: the constitutive cognition is DOXA / KRISIS (belief/judgment), NOT phantasia
concepts.gloss: Fortenbaugh's emotion-cognition is 'opinion', 'judgment', 'propositional judgment open to reasoned logos' (p.48 n.1). Phantasia/imagination/appearance are absent from his apparatus and subject index. [CLUSTER-AXIS KEYSTONE: extreme doxastic pole.]

concepts.label: emotion is open to reason and rhetorical persuasion
concepts.gloss: Because grounded in a belief that argument can criticize and alter, emotion is 'intelligent behaviour'; the angry are not victims of an irrational force. Basis of the Rhetoric's emotional appeal as coordinate with demonstration.

concepts.label: emotion vs. bodily drive (cognitive cause vs. physiological cause)
concepts.gloss: Emotions (anger, fear) have a cognitive efficient cause; bodily drives (hunger, thirst, sex) have a physiological efficient cause and are shared with animals. The dividing line of the whole cognitivist program.

concepts.label: rational vs. non-rational appetite
concepts.gloss: Rhet. 1370a18-25: non-rational appetite originates 'through the body', not from judgment; rational appetite is 'attributed to persuasion'. Lets temperance be a virtue (acquired, judgment-caused 'loves and hates') without reducing it to retuned physiology.

concepts.label: bipartite political-ethical psychology (alogical vs. logical half)
concepts.gloss: Soul divided into an emotional/alogical half (obedient) and a calculative/logical half; ALL emotion located in the alogical half, which is itself COGNITIVE. Replaces Platonic tripartition; underwrites moral-virtue/phronesis distinction.

concepts.label: the alogical half is cognitive (not sensation)
concepts.gloss: The crucial guard: the alogical half is NOT the De Anima's biological faculty of sensation; it bears opinions/assessments and is 'open to reason'. The political-ethical psychology must not be conflated with the biological psychology.

concepts.label: moral virtue (hexis) as perfection of the emotional half; a peculiarly human virtue
concepts.gloss: Moral virtue = a stochastic hexis disposing one to feel/respond at the mean; concerns emotions and actions (EN 1106b15-18); unavailable to beasts, who lack doxa.

concepts.label: virtuous action without calculation (the unreflective critical act)
concepts.gloss: EN 1117a18-22: in sudden alarms the well-trained alogical half assesses correctly and acts without deliberation; hitting the mean is a quick, logos-less critical/cognitive act (eustochia). The nearest Fortenbaughian analogue to a sub-deliberative value-cognition.

concepts.label: moral virtue makes the END correct; practical wisdom the MEANS
concepts.gloss: EN 1144a7-9: anti-Humean division — habituated opinions of the alogical half set the noble goal; phronesis/cleverness selects means. Moral virtue CAN furnish a true judgment of the end (contra Allan).

concepts.label: practical vs. non-practical emotions
concepts.gloss: Practical emotions (fear->safety, anger->revenge) build a goal into the essence and ground action-virtues; non-practical (shame, indignation, pity) carry no essential goal/action and ground no virtue (hence no virtue of mercy/righteous indignation).

concepts.label: the cognition is propositional and object-directed
concepts.gloss: Belief has an object, so anger is necessarily directed at a particular individual (Cleon, Callias; 1378a33-34, 1382a5-6); emotions are individuated by their propositional content (insult vs. harm vs. disgrace).

concepts.label: emotion under demonstrative science (cognition as syllogistic middle term)
concepts.gloss: Post. An.: knowing essence = knowing cause; emotional response gets a syllogistic explanation with the cognition as middle term ('apparent insult' replaces 'unprovoked aggression', 94b16-118).

concepts.label: inclusive (cognitive + bodily) analysis of emotion; homoeopathic katharsis
concepts.gloss: The definition includes material (boiling blood) and final (revenge) cause alongside the efficient (cognitive) cause; the bodily side grounds a quasi-medical theory of purgation of pity and fear (Poet. 1449b27-28; Pol. 1341b32-1342a15).

concepts.label: animals lack emotion/virtue/akrasia (the DOXA-based denial)
concepts.gloss: Animal discrimination is aisthesis+krisis but only 'quasi-affirmation/denial' (De An. 431a9-10), never a doxa 'open to persuasive logos'; so beasts have neither emotions proper, moral virtue, nor akrasia. The belief-based ground for the animal-exclusion.

concepts.label: judgment arouses the body, not vice versa (cognition-first appetite)
concepts.gloss: Even sexual desire is 'often caused by thoughts and beliefs' — desire awakened by the thought that someone is beautiful/worth having (p.87); the strongest case that appetite can be raised into the cognitive register.

concepts.label: De Anima marginalizes emotion (no single biological locus)
concepts.gloss: Fear brings nous+aisthesis+orexis into play at once (p.28 n.1), so emotion fits no single De Anima faculty — partly why the biological work 'ignores' pathos and the Rhetoric must supply the account.

readings.thesis: Aristotle's decisive advance over Plato is to make a THOUGHT/BELIEF the efficient cause named in the essential definition of each emotion (anger = pain dia an apparent unjust slight), resolving the Academic puzzle the Philebus left open.
The constitutive cognition is doxa/krisis — a propositional belief 'open to the persuasion of reasoned logos' — not a phantasia-appearance; phantasia is not a category Fortenbaugh employs.
readings.axis: DOXASTIC<->PHANTASTIC: doxastic (cluster keystone; sets the pole Moss opposes)

readings.thesis: Because the cognition is constitutive, emotion is intelligent and persuasion-responsive: emotional appeal in the Rhetoric is rehabilitated from Gorgianic 'enchantment' to a means coordinate with demonstration; poetic emotions (pity/fear/laughter) are intelligent responses, dissolving Republic X.

Emotions are sharply distinct from non-rational bodily drives: emotion has a cognitive efficient cause, drive a physiological one; but temperance survives as a virtue via rational appetite (judgment-caused 'loves and hates'), and even sexual desire is often cognition-caused.
readings.axis: emotion<->drive: emotion raised into the cognitive register

readings.thesis: The cognitivist analysis grounds a bipartite (alogical/logical) political-ethical psychology that REPLACES tripartition and must NOT be conflated with the De Anima's biological sensation/intellect psychology; the alogical half is itself cognitive.

Moral virtue can operate WITHOUT practical wisdom: in sudden alarms the well-trained alogical half makes a quick, logos-less critical act (eustochia) that hits the mean; the 'right reason' formula concerns reason's authority in justification, not its presence in every virtuous act.

Moral virtue makes the END correct, practical wisdom the MEANS (the anti-Humean reading): the alogical half's habituated opinions can furnish a true judgment of the goal, against Allan's claim that an 'emotional disposition' cannot judge the end.

Practical emotions (with an essential goal) ground action-virtues; non-practical emotions (shame, indignation, pity) ground none — explaining Aristotle's lack of a virtue of righteous indignation and of any analogue to Christian mercy.
readings.axis: scope of moral virtue over the emotion-field

readings.thesis: Emotions, moral virtue, and (by implication) akrasia are denied to animals because animals lack doxa 'open to persuasive logos'; animal pursuit/flight is only 'quasi-affirmation/denial'.

aes_internal: FOUNDATIONAL ORIGIN POINT (1975): pre-dates all other cluster units; cited/engaged BY the later literature rather than citing it. Fortenbaugh's own 'Aristotle's Rhetoric on Emotions' (AGPh 52, 1970) and 'Aristotle: Animals, Emotion and Moral Virtue' supply the esto/causal-definition groundwork the book consolidates.
is_ancestor_of: aes-05 Dow (2015) — Dow's 'affirmation' reading is a refinement/defense of Fortenbaugh's belief-thesis under recalcitrance pressure
aes-02 Konstan (2006) — shares the judgment-thesis and animal/child denial, but socializes the cognition
opposed_by: aes-03 Moss (2009) & aes-04 Moss (2012) — the non-judgmental/phantastic pole directly opposes Fortenbaugh's extreme-doxastic reading; the recalcitrance cases (foot-wide sun, etc.) are unanswerable from within his belief-only apparatus
cross_pipeline: Phantasia Secondary cluster (Nussbaum, Caston, Frede): Fortenbaugh's near-total SILENCE on phantasia is the contrastive datum; his De-Anima-marginalizes-emotion point (p.28 n.1) bears on where the pathe live in Aristotle's psychology
Heidegger BCAP: pathos as being-taken / doxa as yes-saying — Fortenbaugh's doxa-as-efficient-cause is the analytic counterpart to the Heideggerian doxa-as-ratification frame

tensions.desc: Fortenbaugh reads every phainomenon in the Rhetoric definitions ('apparent slight', 'appearance of evil', shame's 'appear likely') as a doxa/thought, never marking the gap between its-appearing-that-p and believing-that-p — the very gap Moss exploits. His belief-only reading is exegetically confident but leaves the recalcitrance phenomena untheorized.

'Virtuous action without calculation' (Ch.4 §2) posits a quick, logos-less critical act of the alogical half that hits the mean — a sub-deliberative evaluative cognition that Fortenbaugh insists is still JUDGMENT, yet which structurally resembles a non-deliberative appearing-good. He has no category (phantasia) to name it, so it strains the doxa-only framework.

Fortenbaugh is the dissertation's foundational ally for the doxa-thesis, but a PURELY doxastic one: he grounds emotion in belief, not appearance, and does not engage the phantasia rival. So the ally confirms the cognitivist pedigree yet supplies no defense against Moss; the dissertation cannot lean on Fortenbaugh to answer recalcitrance — only to establish the lineage.

Fortenbaugh's unreflective critical act (the 'more courageous man') is the cognitivist analogue to the dissertation's lower (basic-tonality) tier — but he reads even THAT tier as cognitive/judgmental, pushing back on conceding the lower tier to a belief-INDEPENDENT phantastic model. He is the witness that the lower tier was classically read as proto-doxastic assessment.

Fortenbaugh denies emotion/virtue/akrasia to animals on a DOXA-based ground (no opinion open to persuasive logos), where Moss denies animal akrasia on a PHANTASIA-based ground (phantasia but no universal). The dissertation must choose which rationale for the animal-exclusion it adopts; the two are not equivalent.

dissertation_hooks.T1-2: FOUNDATIONAL ALLY and the belief/cognitivist pedigree the doxa-thesis descends from — but determinately PURELY DOXASTIC: grounds emotion in doxa/krisis, with phantasia absent from his apparatus and subject index (entry: 'opinion (thought, belief involved in emotion)'; gloss: 'propositional judgments open to reasoned logos', p.48 n.1). Tells the dissertation its strongest historical ally is belief-based, not phantasia-friendly, and pre-dates/does-not-engage the recalcitrance problem.
dissertation_hooks.two-tier: His 'virtuous action without calculation' (the unreflective critical act of the alogical half, EN 1117a18-22) is the cognitivist analogue of the dissertation's lower tier — read by Fortenbaugh as proto-doxastic ASSESSMENT, resisting a belief-independent phantastic construal of that tier.
dissertation_hooks.emotion-vs-appetite: Rational vs. non-rational appetite (Rhet. 1370a18-25) + 'judgment arouses the body, not vice versa' (even sexual desire cognition-caused, p.87) arm the dissertation's epithymia discussion: the judgmental camp's principled way to RAISE appetite into the cognitive register.
dissertation_hooks.animal-pathos: DOXA-based denial of animal emotion/virtue/akrasia (animal pursuit = 'quasi-affirmation', De An. 431a9-10) — the belief-based complement to Moss's phantasia-based animal-exclusion; the dissertation must pick a rationale.
dissertation_hooks.effect-of-emotion-on-judgment: Fortenbaugh's direction is judgment->emotion (belief grounds emotion), registering emotion->judgment only glancingly (emotions 'upset reasoning', make men deliberate about means). Confirms the emotion-DISTORTS-cognition arc of the pathetic loop is a phantastic-camp contribution, not a founding-doxastic one.
